message: fix(contract): a producer takes the ids its rule owns, so ownership is checked at the call site

edits.find: export type EveryRuleIdIsGrouped<Ungrouped extends never = UngroupedRuleId> = Ungrouped;
edits.replace:
export type EveryRuleIdIsGrouped<Ungrouped extends never = UngroupedRuleId> = Ungrouped;

/**
 * The `ids` argument list a producer takes, derived from the rule id it was handed.
 *
 * `asDiagnostic` takes a `RuleId` and an `ids` that are independent of each other, so a call naming
 * an idless rule and passing a payload compiled and produced a diagnostic `Diagnostic` calls
 * unrepresentable. That assertion cannot be removed: TypeScript does not narrow a union by a
 * discriminant it knows only the type of, and a producer holding its rule id as data holds exactly
 * that. What can be removed is every call site reaching it while naming its rule by a literal, and a
 * producer spreading this is what removes them. A rule that owns no ids takes no argument, a rule
 * that always names them requires one, and a rule whose sites disagree, or a rule id known only as
 * `RuleId`, leaves it optional.
 *
 * Each `extends` is guarded by a one-element tuple, and the guard is load-bearing rather than a
 * spelling. A naked conditional distributes over a union, so `OwnedIds<RuleId>` would answer once
 * per member and collapse to the union of all three lists, which is every existing caller broken
 * rather than one boundary left open. Guarded, the open case answers once and answers optional,
 * which is what a producer forwarding a `RuleId` needs.
 *
 * `EveryRuleIdIsGrouped` is read rather than trusted, and that read is the half it was missing. A
 * rule in no group would otherwise reach the optional list by failing both tests, which is the one
 * wrong answer this type can give and the one a reader would never suspect. Reading the partition
 * turns it into a build failure at every producer instead, and it also stops that proof being a gate
 * a later reader could delete while believing it was dead: it failed the build only at its own
 * declaration before this, so nothing went red when it was removed. The run-time partition case in
 * `rule-id.test.ts` is not a second mechanism beside it; that case reads the arrays and this states
 * the claim about the type. See ADR-097 and issue #449.
 */
export type OwnedIds<Rule extends RuleId> = [EveryRuleIdIsGrouped] extends [never]
  ? [Rule] extends [IdlessRuleId]
    ? []
    : [Rule] extends [IdentifiedRuleId]
      ? [ids: readonly string[]]
      : [ids?: readonly string[]]
  : [ungrouped: never];

edits.find: Ownership of `ids` is enforced where the rule id is known and asserted where it is not, and that boundary is worth stating rather than implying. A diagnostic built from a literal rule id, or from one already narrowed to a group as `publishFailureRule` narrows its answer, is checked against its variant by the compiler. The five producers that accept an open `RuleId` cannot be: TypeScript does not narrow a union by a discriminant it knows only the type of, so each passes through one assertion in `contract/diagnostics.ts`, backed by the measurement in `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` rather than by a proof. Closing that needs those producers to take their `ids` as a rest tuple derived from the rule id they were handed, so a call naming a rule that owns no ids cannot pass one and a call naming a rule that always names ids cannot omit them. That is a slice of its own, because it rewrites every call site of five constructors, and the scope of this record is the union and the discrimination.
edits.replace: Ownership of `ids` is enforced at the producer, and the boundary that remains is worth stating rather than implying. A diagnostic built from a literal rule id, or from one already narrowed to a group as `publishFailureRule` narrows its answer, is checked against its variant by the compiler. The five producers that accept an open `RuleId` still pass through one assertion in `contract/diagnostics.ts`, because TypeScript does not narrow a union by a discriminant it knows only the type of; what changed is that nothing reaches that assertion unchecked any more. Each of the five takes its `ids` as `OwnedIds` of the rule id it was handed, so a call naming a rule that owns no ids cannot pass one and a call naming a rule that always names ids cannot omit them. The derivation is guarded by a one-element tuple on each side of `extends`, because a naked conditional distributes over `RuleId` and would answer with the union of all three lists, which is every existing caller broken rather than one boundary left open. What the compiler still cannot answer for is a producer forwarding a rule id it holds as data: `contract/validate-v5.ts` through `scopedRuleId`, whose two scopes are both idless, and `runtime/report.ts` through the private `frozenDiagnostic`, which is reached only from the exported member that now derives its own list. Those two are the assertion's whole remaining subject, and both are backed by the measurement in `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` rather than by a proof.
